provenance.title: Physics-Guided Motion Loss for Video Generation Model
provenance.abstract: Current video diffusion models generate visually compelling content but often violate basic laws of physics, producing subtle artifacts like rubber-sheet deformations and inconsistent object motion. We introduce a frequency-domain physics prior that improves motion plausibility without modifying model architectures.
key_claims: Frequency-domain physics prior improves motion plausibility without changing backbone architecture
Only 2.7% of spectral coefficients are needed while preserving 97%+ of spectral energy
Average ~11% relative improvement in motion accuracy and action recognition on OpenVID-1M
User studies show 74–83% preference for physics-enhanced videos
Reduces warping error by 22–37% depending on backbone

architecture.description: Drop-in frequency-domain regularizer applied during diffusion training. No backbone modification. Plugs into standard denoising objective as an auxiliary loss on the reconstructed x̂₀.

components.name: 3D FFT Low-Pass Module
components.operation: 3D Discrete Fourier Transform followed by low-pass cube truncation (ϱ=0.3 per dimension)
components.input: [T, H, W] video window (one channel; RGB handled channel-wise)
components.output: Truncated spectral cube — only 2.7% of coefficients (low-frequency cube)
components.notes: Separable: 2D spatial DFT per frame + 1D temporal DFT with optional Hann window. Retains 97–98.7% of spectral energy under natural video power-law (κ≈1.8).

components.name: Translational Motion Loss (ℒ_trans)
components.operation: Energy-weighted ridge WLS plane fitting in (ωx, ωy, ωt) space
components.input: Spectral cube; design matrix rows Aᵢ = (ωx,i, ωy,i, 1), bᵢ = -ωt,i
components.output: Scalar loss: normalized WLS residual from plane ωt + vx·ωx + vy·ωy + b₀ = 0
components.notes: Velocity estimate β̂_tr via ridge-WLS (λ=1e-3). Loss = Σ Wᵢᵢ(Aᵢβ̂-bᵢ)² / Σ Wᵢᵢ

components.name: Rotational Motion Loss (ℒ_rot)
components.operation: Polar resampling → angular DFT → temporal DFT; ring concentration + tilted-line energy ratio
components.input: Spectral cube resampled to polar (ρ, θ); angular harmonics Cₘ(ρ,t)

sub_components.tilted_line_ratio: C_rot = E_line / E_all  where E_line sums |C̃ₘ|² within |ωt + mΩ*| ≤ Δ
sub_components.ring_concentration: C_ring = 1 - H̄_ring / log(Nr)  where H̄_ring is mean temporal entropy over Nr rings

components.name: Scaling Motion Loss (ℒ_scale)
components.operation: Log-radius resampling of spatial frequency plane; radial-flow alignment + centroid trend
components.input: Ring energies Ek(t) per concentric annulus in spatial-frequency plane

sub_components.flow_alignment: C_flow = |Σ ∇̂ρE · ∇̂tE| — absolute dot product of normalized radial vs temporal energy gradients
sub_components.centroid_trend: S_trend = |corr(ρc, t)| — Pearson correlation of radial spectral centroid over time

components.name: Adaptive Weighting Module
components.operation: Softmax over negated individual losses with temperature τ
components.output: Scalar composite loss ℒ_motion = Σ w_i · Lᵢ
components.notes: Small τ → winner-takes-all; large τ → uniform mix. Grounded in maximum-entropy principle.

components.name: Backbone Video Diffusion Model (frozen structure)
components.operation: Standard denoising objective; ℒ_motion added as auxiliary loss computed on x̂₀
components.notes: No architectural changes. For Hunyuan: LoRA adapters in attention + time-related linear layers; all other weights frozen.

data_flow: Video window V ∈ R^{T×H×W} → 3D FFT (with Hann window) → V̂(ωx,ωy,ωt)
V̂ → Low-pass cube truncation (ϱ=0.3) → reduced spectral cube
Cube → [ℒ_trans branch]: WLS plane fit in (ωx,ωy,ωt)
Cube → [ℒ_rot branch]: polar resample → angular DFT → temporal DFT → ring entropy + tilted-line ratio
Cube → [ℒ_scale branch]: ring energies → radial gradient alignment + centroid trend
{ℒ_trans, ℒ_rot, ℒ_scale} → Adaptive softmax weighting (τ=0.1) → ℒ_motion
ℒ_motion (weight 0.1) + standard denoising loss → total training objective

unified_sim2_hyperplane.role: Theoretical foundation — ideal SIM(2) motion concentrates all spectral energy on this hyperplane in (ωx, ωy, m, ν, ωt)

translation_plane.role: Spectral support of constant-velocity translational motion — slice of SIM(2) hyperplane

rotation_line.role: Tilted lines in (m, ωt) plane — m-th angular harmonic acquires temporal tone mΩ

scaling_line.role: Tilted lines in (ν, ωt) plane after log-radius transform converts scaling to translation

translational_loss.role: Training loss — normalized WLS plane-fitting residual

angular_velocity_estimate.role: Closed-form energy-weighted LS estimate of rotation rate

components.C_flow: |Σ ∇̂ρE · ∇̂tE|  (absolute dot product of unit gradient fields)
components.S_trend: |corr(ρc, t)|  (Pearson correlation of radial centroid over time)

adaptive_composite_loss.role: Final composite physics loss added to backbone denoising objective

unified_wls_regression.where: φᵢ = [ωx, ωy, m, ν, 1], bᵢ = -ωt, θ = [vx, vy, Ω, α, b₀]ᵀ
unified_wls_regression.role: Gold-standard unified residual fitting — theoretical anchor for all three surrogate losses

retained_energy_fraction.role: Theoretical energy retention bound for low-pass truncation under power-law video spectra

energy_gate.role: Soft gate that down-weights low-energy spectral samples in WLS

observability_gate_rotation.role: Down-weights near-zero angular harmonics where rotation is unobservable

key_theoretical_insights: SIM(2) spectral manifold: any similarity transform (translate + rotate + scale) concentrates all energy on ONE hyperplane ωt + vxωx + vyωy + Ωm + αν + b₀ = 0 in 5D frequency space
Log-radius coordinate change converts scaling from a dilation (hard to detect) to a translation (easy to detect as a tilted line in (ν,ωt))
Low-pass cube with ϱ=0.3 is sufficient: natural video spectra follow ~ω^(-3.6) power law, so >97% energy concentrates in lowest 2.7% of coefficients
Adaptive softmax weighting is maximum-entropy optimal: it automatically selects the dominant motion type without hard classification
All three losses upper-bound the gold-standard unified SIM(2) residual L_uni (proven via Cauchy-Schwarz and Chebyshev inequalities in Appendix B)
